newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS TO BE SPREAD OVER TWO DAYS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-CROSS COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIPS TO BE SPREAD OVER TWO DAYS.

text.p: Next year's world cross country championships are to be staged over two days instead of one, Primo Nebiolo, the International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) president, said on Saturday.
Additional, shorter, races for senior men and women would be also be introduced.
"A one day event does not justify the expense, effort and organisation," said Nebiolo.

The first day on the new schedule will include the junior women's 4-km race and the shorter senior men's and women's races, probably over 4-km and 5-km. The second day's timetable will include the junior men's 8-km race, the senior women's race, which will be extended to 8-km next year, and the senior men's 12-km race.
The news of an additional day will come as a shock to the organisers of next year's championship in Marrakesh, Morocco. Nebiolo acknowledged that they had not be told about the decision.
The change has still to be approved by the IAAF Council, which will meet between May 29-31 in Athens, but that is believed to be a formality.
Nebiolo also said that he hoped future world cross country championships would be staged in city centre sites like Sunday's event in Turin's Parco Del Valentino.
"I believe that cross country has a great tradition but in the past the world championships have been held a little out of the cities and there have been few spectators."
He wondered: "Why can we not we not organise this (the world cross country championships) in London's Hyde Park or Central Park in New York?"

Nebiolo also confirmed that Belfast was still scheduled to be the venue of the 1999 world championships despite speculation that the event was about to be moved in the wake of some renewed terrorist activity in Northern Ireland.
